label: def:breit-wheeler-pair-production
title: Breit--Wheeler pair production (categorical)
html:
The Breit--Wheeler process models categorical pair production, \gamma\gamma \to e^- e^+. Two photons fuse by the product in the Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_3(q):

  \gamma(\varphi) \cdot \gamma(\psi),
  \qquad
  \gamma(\varphi) = \mathbf{1} + \varphi_0\sigma_0 + \varphi_1\sigma_1 + \varphi_{01}\,\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1}.

The electron and positron are the braid words

  e^- = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0  \text{ (closure: Hopf link)}, \qquad
  e^+ = \sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_0^{-1}  \text{ (closure: mirror Hopf link)}.

The e^- channel of the product is its coefficient on \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0, which is \varphi_{01}\psi_0 + \varphi_1\psi_{01}: it needs the vertex term \sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1} of one photon and a single-crossing term of the other. A single crossing \sigma_i is a term of a photon, not a photon, and two bare photons fuse to \gamma(0)\gamma(0) = \mathbf{1}.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall. It invokes real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0. The underlying categorical identities hold over an abstract coefficient ring. Only their archimedean realisation is specialised.
